passage: Friday. Results today. Rituraj came first in the class again, and Ma'am read his name out. I clapped, but my stomach stung like I had swallowed a chilli. I even thought, he just memorises. But I know he does not. On the way home I did not say anything mean, because that would only make me feel worse. At the bus stop I asked, "Rituraj, how did you study for the science test?" He grinned. "I make small question cards and go through them in bed." I am going to make my own cards this weekend. The sting is still there, a little. Kalyani.

qa.q: What does Rituraj make to study for science?
qa.a: He makes small question cards and goes through them in bed.

qa.q: What did Kalyani feel when Rituraj's name was read out?
qa.a: Kalyani felt envy, which Kalyani describes as a sting in the stomach like a chilli, even while clapping.

qa.q: What did Kalyani do that turned envy into something useful?
qa.a: Kalyani asked Rituraj how he studied and planned to make question cards too, instead of running Rituraj down.

qa.q: How might Rituraj have felt when Kalyani asked him how he studied?
qa.a: Rituraj probably felt pleased to be asked and happy to share, and it kept their friendship easy. 😊

grounding: A child feels envy when a friend tops the class and turns it into learning by asking what helped him study.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 6B, results day.
When I read out that Francis had come first, Kalyani, his closest friend, clapped more slowly than the others. At break I heard her tell two girls, 'He only topped because he sits in front and sucks up.' She looked miserable saying it. Later she stayed back and admitted, 'It felt like a punch in my stomach. I wanted to be first.' I told her the sting is normal and shows she cares about doing well, but that running Francis down would hurt them both. I suggested she ask him how he revised. At lunch I saw them together, Francis drawing a revision timetable in her notebook. Kalyani was nodding.

qa.q: Who came first in the class?
What was Kalyani feeling when she said Francis only topped because he sucks up?
qa.a: Envious and miserable; it felt like a punch in the stomach because she wanted to be first.

qa.q: What did the teacher suggest, and what did Kalyani do?
qa.a: To ask Francis how he revised; at lunch he drew a revision timetable in her notebook.

qa.q: How might Francis feel if he heard Kalyani's comment?
qa.a: Hurt and confused that his closest friend had run him down.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a girl envious of her friend topping the class, and turning envy into learning from him.

passage:
Thursday
Diary, it's Samir. Jatin topped the whole class in science. Ninety-eight! When Ma'am said his name, I felt a sharp jab in my belly, like I'd swallowed a wasp. I got eighty-one. We study together every Sunday, so how? At lunch I almost told Akash that Jatin probably saw the paper early. I stopped halfway, because that was mean and not even true. Then I felt worse. After school I asked Jatin straight out, 'What did you do differently?' He said he made his own quiz cards and tested himself every night instead of just reading. He even offered to make some for me. I'm still a bit jealous. But I'm going to try the cards. On Sunday we're making them together.

qa.q: What did Jatin make to study?
How did Samir feel when Ma'am said Jatin's name?
qa.a: A sharp jab of envy in the belly, like having swallowed a wasp.

qa.q: What turned Samir's envy into something useful?
qa.a: Asking Jatin what he did differently and planning to try his quiz-card method.

qa.q: How did Jatin respond to Samir's question?
qa.a: Generously; he explained his method and offered to make cards for Samir.

grounding: A child stung by envy when a friend tops the class stops short of running him down and asks what helped him study.
